text: The after-action report is a different document from the risk register you updated last lesson. The register tracks this risk forward in time. The AAR is a one-time record of exactly what happened, written now, while the details are still fresh enough to teach something.

The real timeline: an audit reporting 12 standing admins, an automation run four days later flagging 5 accounts the audit's group-membership query could never see, and root cause confirmed two days after that — a methodology gap, not a data error. Both counts were accurate for what each method actually checked.

What went right: the automation's dual-check design caught exactly the kind of gap it was built to catch. What went wrong: five break-glass grants from a March emergency were never formally revoked, because nothing enforced their own cleanup once the emergency closed.

Four corrective actions close this out, each with a named owner and a real due date — rewriting the audit query, migrating break-glass access to a managed workflow platform-wide, a recurring stale-grant sweep, and formalizing the dual-check as the standing validation layer. Next lesson takes this story to the board.
